method.presses: Every press is a real locator.click(). No element.click() and no dispatchEvent is used for a press.
method.pressLog: A read-only init script records mousedown, mouseup, click (window, capture phase) and pointerlockchange, each with whether document.pointerLockElement was set. "reached" means the click was delivered to the pressed control; "capturedBeforeClick" means the pointer was captured at some moment from mousedown to that delivery.

adapters.synchronous: The collector's three overrides, unchanged (cases of the first six, the banner cases, the wave Skip case, the empty-box case).
adapters.synchronousSilentRelease: Same synchronous grant, but exitPointerLock() fires pointerlockchange only when it ends a lock, as a browser does (the paused Skip case). The collector's adapter fires it on every release and cannot show a state that depends on no event arriving.
adapters.limits: Both are models. Neither redirects the rest of a press to the lock element the way a real browser does once a lock is granted, so a click on a control that stays visible is always delivered here. A real browser was not used: headless Chromium grants no pointer lock.

setupShortenedFromPageScript.killcam: a Skip press after a wave death: A live enemy is assigned to player.lastAttacker and the game's own triggerDeath() is called. The death is not played out.
setupShortenedFromPageScript.killcam: a Skip press while paused at a: A live enemy is assigned to player.lastAttacker and the TDM mode's own tick is called once with 601 seconds, so the match ends on time, lost 0 to 0 with the player alive, and the end-of-match killcam starts.
setupShortenedFromPageScript.note: In both cases the press on #kc-skip itself is a real click. The banner cases use no page-script setup: the join fails because the owned Vite server has no game server behind it.

reading: Without the whole guard the first case fails exactly as in the original RED record (#overlay hidden), so the served variant reproduces the frozen behaviour and the mechanism is a valid stand-in for it.

Without the whole guard a press on the empty part of the pause box hides the menu and captures the pointer. With the registered guard it does neither. This is the behaviour change the review ruled acceptable; it is now pinned by a case.

Without #kc-skip in the guard, a Skip press after a wave death is delivered, but the pointer is captured on the press and stays captured on the KILLED IN ACTION screen (pointerLocked true at the end). With #kc-skip guarded the same case passes. This is the first browser evidence for that half of the selector.

Without #kc-skip in the guard, the paused Skip case ends clean (result shown, pause menu hidden, pointer released) and fails only on the press observation: the pointer was captured before the click. So the review's reading is confirmed: before this plan the stale pause menu was cleared by the lock and unlock cycle of the press.

F-01.how: Online TDM pressed with no game server: the banner appears. Offline TDM is then started through its button and the pointer released: the banner is still visible over the running match, with the pause menu.
F-01.onCurrentSource: A real press on Retry or on Return to menu captures the pointer on mousedown (capturedBeforeClick true). Under this adapter the click is still delivered, because the banner is not hidden by pointerlockchange: Return to menu returned to the menu and hid the banner, Retry made a second matchmaking request and ended with the banner up and the pointer released.
F-01.reading: The lock-on-press mechanism of the Main Menu defect reproduces on both banner buttons. The lost click does not reproduce under this adapter, and whether a real browser loses it was not measured.

F-02.waveSkip: Passes on current source. Fails without #kc-skip in the guard: the pointer stays captured on the death screen.
F-02.pausedSkipAtRoundEnd: Fails on current source: #pause-menu stays visible over #snd-result. Ends clean without #kc-skip in the guard. This is a regression introduced by the registered state and is not left in place.
